intro: Look up. Sumela Monastery, in Trabzon province, clings to a 300-metre cliff above the Altındere valley. Its story begins in the 4th century AD, and at its heart lies a rock church covered with frescoes, inside and out.
history: The monastery was founded in the fourth century, but it owes most of its present form to the thirteenth, under the Empire of Trebizond. It began as a natural cave turned into a church, and over the centuries it grew into a five-storey complex. Ottoman sultans confirmed its privileges by decree. Then, in the population exchange of 1923, it was emptied.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Rock Church and its frescoed inner and outer walls, then the students' rooms, the library and the aqueduct.
facts: Did you know? The outer wall of the rock church is frescoed too. The paintings were carried outside the building so that those who could not get in could still follow the liturgy from without. The monastery is pressed against a cliff 300 metres above the valley floor, and it is reached only by the path that climbs the slope. And the Ottoman sultans who confirmed its privileges by decree included Selim I.
outro: This brings our tour of Sumela Monastery to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This monastery has held on to its cliff for centuries; let it keep holding on for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
